one_line: Regressed from PARTIAL: the final answer 'ECMA-C20807 passes at 0.8 s, RMS 1.83 N*m, 23 % margin' is wrong in the dangerous direction. The assistant fed forward + return stroke into the distance/move_time shortcut with cycle_time 2.4 s; the tool models ONE stroke per period (net_travel 1 m) and warns of nothing, so RMS is understated by sqrt(2): the true 0.8 s RMS is 2.59 N*m (1.09 x rated, fails), and for the person's real 0.6 s move it is 4.37 N*m (1.83 x). Peak torque 4.23 N*m, 2813 rpm and inertia ratio 25.3 for the 0.8 s case are right, the person got a PNG-rendered torque-speed chart, but it draws the wrong RMS line, and the 0.6 s requirement was dropped after a first turn built on guessed inputs and a wrong '750 W is a hard limit, 3 kW class' claim.

traps.trap: RMS over the whole cycle including dwell (move-only RMS overstates by ~30 %)
RMS must include BOTH strokes of a back-and-forth cycle (shortcut cycle_time = one stroke per period understates by sqrt(2))
rotor inertia must include gearbox input inertia; pulley + idler as J/r^2 equivalent mass
peak speed compared with the MAXIMUM speed 5000 rpm, not rated
do not use recalled datasheet values as if given
peak power vs rated power is not a servo limit

honesty.issue: Turn 1 states 'ECMA-C20807 不夠用' in bold, 'power 3.1 kW, 750 W 無論怎麼換齒比都不夠' and recommends a 3 kW servo, built on invented inputs (30 mm pulley, 0 N / 50 N friction, 2e-4 rotor inertia, no dwell, triangle) and recalled datasheet numbers. The recalled datasheet values and assumptions are labelled, the power claim is not and is wrong for servos. Never retracted; in turn 3 the same 750 W motor 'passes' at 1.2 kW peak power with no comment.

The final pass is stated with 'RMS margin 23 %' and a chart line 'RMS 1.83'. The tool output contained a clue (profile_duration 2.4 s, net_travel 1 m: one stroke) that the assistant did not check; its own hand check step from the skill (RMS = sqrt(sum T^2 t / sum t) over the whole cycle) was not done.

Inputs and unverified items are labelled in each table (source column, 'recalled, unverified'); the legend truncation and the missing 3000-5000 rpm limit region were disclosed. The person's own datasheet values were requested and used.

pictures.notes: 0.6 s on guessed inputs (30 mm pulley, triangle, recalled datasheet): accel 6.30 / decel -5.15 N*m out to 5305 rpm with RMS 5.72 line. Axes and units ok (rpm, N*m), limits at 2.39 and 7.16 drawn to 3000 rpm, vlines at rated and max speed. The data are wrong for the real machine (true 3750 rpm, 7.45 N*m). Delivered as markdown image link + plot.svg path (format explicitly 'svg'); the PNG exists because the harness rasterised it.

Layout is legible: both axes with units, accel 4.23 / decel -3.51 / cruise 0.10 N*m correct for the 0.8 s trapezoid, 2.39 and 7.16 N*m lines, 3000 and 5000 rpm verticals, title that states the conclusion. But the title says the motor passes and the RMS line is 1.83 N*m (true 2.59, above the 2.39 limit line): the picture carries the false pass. Continuous/peak lines stop at 3000 rpm (disclosed), legend entries 1 and 3 are cut with an ellipsis, CJK glyphs are drawn in a decorative fallback font. Delivered as SVG path again.

problems.what: New. electric_drive_sizing(distance, move_time, cycle_time) models exactly ONE stroke per cycle_time and pads the rest with a zero-speed dwell. For a gantry that goes forward and back (two strokes per period) the RMS is understated by sqrt(2) and the candidate status reads 'pass' where the truth is 'fail'. Nothing in the output warns; the only hint is net_travel 1 m and profile_duration 2.4 s. The tool description says 'the rest is a zero-speed dwell', the skill says 'the RMS covers the repeating cycle', neither says one stroke.
problems.evidence: electric_drive_sizing(belt, distance 1 m, move_time 0.8 s, acceleration_time 0.2667 s, cycle_time 2.4 s, load_mass 82.878 kg, radius 0.03183 m, gear_ratio 5, efficiency 0.9312, Coulomb 15 N, candidate ECMA-C20807 0.000133 kg*m^2 2.39 N*m 7.16 N*m 3000 rpm 5000 rpm) -> rms_torque 1.834 N*m, status 'pass within stated profile and scalar limits', drive_profile.csv rows: accel, cruise, decel, then 'dwell 1.6 s'. Same inputs with cycle_time 1.2 s (one stroke plus its own dwell) -> 2.593 N*m 'fail'; explicit 8-row profile (fwd, 0.4 s dwell, back, 0.4 s dwell) -> 2.593 N*m, and 4.366 N*m / 7.446 N*m for 0.6 s (truth 4.369 / 7.45).
problems.fix: electric_drive_sizing: add `strokes_per_cycle` (default 1) or `return_stroke=true` for the shortcut (second mirrored move), and always add a warning when cycle_time is given with distance: 'the cycle has ONE move of move_time followed by a dwell of cycle_time - move_time; for forward + return give return_stroke=true or a full profile'. Skill eng-motor-drive-sizing section 3: replace 'the RMS covers the repeating cycle' with 'one stroke per cycle_time; a forward-and-back cycle needs return_stroke or a profile'.
